findings.title: Organization slug condition is inverted after the `!` was dropped
findings.description: The hunk at `@@ -148` changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. The original included the plain `slug` when billing was disabled. The new code includes it only when billing is enabled, so the behavior is reversed. The adjacent `requestedSlug` line keeps the original polarity, which makes the flip look accidental.

findings.title: Unguarded `.integration` access will throw when there is no destination calendar
findings.description: The Google Meet fallback now reads `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then checks `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. When `destinationCalendar` is null or empty, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and the property read throws a TypeError. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which did not throw. The access needs `?.`.

findings.title: Google `updateEvent` searches for the calendar using the falsy `externalCalendarId`
findings.description: The new fallback is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. In the `else` branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares against a falsy value and almost always returns `undefined`. The lookup should match on something other than the value that already failed the truthiness check.

findings.title: Google `deleteEvent` has the same falsy-lookup problem
findings.description: `calendarId` is now `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This has the same issue as the update path: when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the `find` almost never matches, so delete falls through to `"primary"` or fails.

findings.title: The `|| []` fallback for `eventType.users` was dropped
findings.description: The old expression ended with `: eventType.users || [];`. The new code returns `users.length ? users : eventType.users;`. If `eventType.users` is optional, `loadUsers` can now return `undefined`, and the later `users.length` and `users.slice` calls will throw.

findings.title: An empty `dynamicUserList` is now rejected, and the message is replaced by a generic 500
findings.description: The new guard throws a plain `Error` for an empty `dynamicUserList`. The `catch` only maps `HttpError` and Prisma errors to a 400 with the message. A plain `Error` becomes a 500 with "Unable to load users", so the descriptive message is lost. Empty dynamic lists were not rejected before this change, so this is also a behavior change to confirm.
